whatItIs.text: Cyprus's squeaky, high-melting-point cheese that fries and grills without melting — the reason it is the vegetarian 'meat' of the grill.

historyNote.text: Halloumi is thought to have been first made by Bedouins whose nomadic life suited its keeping qualities; Cypriot records call it 'calumi' around 1554, and its name may trace back to a word for cheese in 2nd-century Roman Egypt.

howToChoose.text: Buy blocks in brine and check the milk mix — traditional sheep-and-goat versions taste rounder, while cow's-milk-heavy ones (now most exports) are milder.

storage.text: Keep sealed in its brine in the fridge.

useItUp.text: Slice thin, pat dry, and fry hard for the best crust; leftover halloumi crisps into salads and wraps, and tired pieces still grate into fritters.

substitutions.note: won't fry solid — crumble instead; saltier
